title: OnCo gap census, November 2026
corpus: src/data at main 0114cef1b plus public/api/v1/all.ndjson built 2026-11-04 13:35 (21,337 records)
method: Taxonomy of 174 object types in 12 families built before searching; for each type the best outside denominators (machine-readable first), enumerated on 4 November 2026; every item diffed against src/data by name, alias, brand, code and identifier; types ranked by gap severity x reader impact; a random 30 gaps re-checked against the corpus and their sources.

statusLegend.MENTION: named in passing in src/data, no record is about it

precision.automatedRegrep: 27/30 (3 explained: short-alias false hit, side-table gap on an existing record, trial-title-only name)

types.name: Hospices and cancer support centres
types.oncoMethod: Individual centres and hospices: none found. incorpus.py on the 32 Maggie's centres and 9 Marie Curie hospices returned MISSING for every one. Network-level organisations are present instead: maggies-centres (collection), cancer-support-community (collection), acs-hope-lodge (collection), marie-curie-uk (institution), macmillan-cancer-support, penny-brohn-uk, teenage-cancer-trust, young-lives-vs-cancer, ronald-mcdonald-house-charities, look-good-feel-better, cancer-council-australia (11 network records), plus assistance-schemes.ts rows for Maggie's and Hope Lodge.

denominators.name: Maggie's: Our centres
denominators.notes: 32 centre pages linked (/our-centres/maggies-<place>/): 29 in the UK plus Groningen, Hong Kong and Tokyo.

denominators.name: Marie Curie: hospices
denominators.notes: Redirects to /services/hospices; 9 hospice pages: Belfast, Bradford, Cardiff, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Hampstead, Liverpool, Newcastle, West Midlands.

denominators.name: Cancer Support Community: Find a location near you
denominators.notes: Page states 'our global community of support is found at over 200 locations including Cancer Support Community, Gilda's Club, and healthcare partners'; the location list is an interactive map, only 2 location links in the HTML.

denominators.name: Hospice UK: hospice care finder
denominators.notes: Page reads 'Our hospice finder shows you adult and children's hospices near you'; the finder itself was not enumerated.

denominators.name: St Christopher's Hospice history page
denominators.notes: Not read.

coverage.method: Individual centres from two enumerated lists (Maggie's 32 + Marie Curie hospices 9) run through incorpus.py with and without the apostrophe: 0 matched. Network level, separately: of 10 support and hospice networks checked (Maggie's, Cancer Support Community, Gilda's Club, ACS Hope Lodge, Marie Curie, Sue Ryder, Hospice UK, NHPCO, Teenage Cancer Trust, Macmillan), 6 have a record, 3 are mentions (Gilda's Club, Hospice UK, NHPCO) and 1 is missing (Sue Ryder).
coverage.caveats: OnCo models support as national networks, which suits a reader looking for a helpline, but a reader looking for the centre or hospice near them finds nothing. US hospices (thousands) and the 200+ CSC/Gilda's Club sites were not enumerable as lists.

notEnumerated: US hospices and the NHPCO membership: no machine-readable list fetched (CMS Hospice Compare provider data would be the denominator; not attempted).
Cancer Support Community and Gilda's Club locations (200+ stated): interactive map only.
ACS Hope Lodge locations, Teenage Cancer Trust hospital units, Young Lives vs Cancer Homes from Home, Cancer Council lodges: network records exist; site lists not fetched.
St Christopher's Hospice: site returned 403; it is named in OnCo only inside Cicely Saunders' record.
Children's hospices and hospices outside the UK and US: not attempted.
types.notes: Hospice and support charities as organisations overlap with worktree-agent-a2b1ed541c1d2d610 (charities via IRS and Charity Commission registers); individual centres and hospices are facilities and are not in that agent's scope.

types.name: Patient advocacy groups
types.oncoMethod: Collections tagged patient-org (28): mostly US disease foundations (ACS, LLS, PanCAN, MMRF, LRF, NBTS, ALSF, St Baldrick's, Colorectal Cancer Alliance, LUNGevity/GO2, MRA, OCRA, Komen, PCF, FORCE, Sharsheret ...) and UK support charities (Maggie's, Penny Brohn, Young Lives vs Cancer); plus UK disease charities stored as institutions with the charity tag (Pancreatic Cancer UK, Breast Cancer Now, Bowel Cancer UK, AMMF, Roy Castle, Prostate Cancer UK, Lymphoma Action, Blood Cancer UK) and FAVO and ELLOK.

denominators.name: EMA eligible patients' and consumers' organisations (oncology subset)
denominators.notes: Of about 45 eligible organisations, 7 are cancer bodies: ECL, Cancer Patients Europe, Europa Uomo, Lung Cancer Europe, Lymphoma Coalition Europe, Myeloma Patients Europe, European MEN Alliance. EURORDIS added for rare cancers.

denominators.name: International and European cancer patient coalitions named in the assignment plus the common disease networks, each verified on its own homepage
denominators.notes: 28 homepages fetched; 26 answered 200 (titles and descriptions recorded in dl-advocacy/results.json). ikcc.org and europadonna.org returned 403, so IKCC and Europa Donna are unverified this session and excluded from the count.

denominators.name: European Cancer Patient Coalition (ECPC) member list
denominators.notes: Both ecpc.org and www.ecpc.org timed out after 40 s. ECPC itself is MISSING from the corpus but could not be verified, so it is not listed as a gap.

coverage.method: incorpus.py on each organisation's name and acronym. None of the 7 EMA-eligible oncology bodies and none of the 26 verified coalitions has a record; 8 are MENTION (CPE, LuCE, MPE, ALK Positive, ROS1ders, EGFR Resisters, KRAS Kickers, plus MET Crusaders, which was not in the denominator), the rest MISSING. European MEN Alliance counted in the denominator but not listed as a gap (low impact).
coverage.caveats: OnCo does hold US national disease foundations; this denominator measures the international and European coalition layer, which is where it has nothing. Target Ovarian Cancer and MDS Alliance homepages answered without readable text and were not used as evidence.

notEnumerated: ECPC's roughly 400 members: site unreachable (timeout)
IKCC and Europa Donna: homepages returned 403; both are MISSING from the corpus but unverified this session
National disease-specific patient groups outside the US and UK (for example the members of Lymphoma Coalition or Myeloma Patients Europe): member lists not fetched
US-based groups in this list (BCAN, KCA, Max Foundation, Life Raft Group, the oncogene groups) may also surface in worktree-agent-a2b1ed541c1d2d610's IRS sweep
types.notes: The biggest structural gap in the family: OnCo has no record for any international or European patient coalition, including the four EMA-eligible disease coalitions (Europa Uomo, Lung Cancer Europe, Lymphoma Coalition Europe, Myeloma Patients Europe) and the oncogene-driven groups that now co-design trials.

types.name: Patient education resources
types.oncoMethod: Individual items from the four outside libraries linked by URL anywhere in src/data (URL index of 39,094 URLs built from every .ts and .json file): 43 NCI PDQ summaries (any version), 3 ESMO Patient Guides, 0 NCCN Guidelines for Patients, 0 ONS/NCODA Patient Education Sheets. At library level OnCo has a collection record for PDQ (cancer-gov-pdq), source collections for Macmillan and CRUK About Cancer (86 Macmillan cancer-information URLs), and names NCCN Guidelines for Patients and ESMO patient guides only in passing.

denominators.name: NCI PDQ Cancer Information Summaries (7 category pages: adult treatment, pediatric treatment, supportive and palliative care, screening, prevention, genetics, integrative therapies)
denominators.notes: 235 unique summaries after merging patient and health-professional versions and the index's cross-reference aliases: adult treatment 82, pediatric 64, supportive 23, screening 19, prevention 16, genetics 7, integrative 24.

denominators.name: ESMO Patient Guides
denominators.notes: Page is a Nuxt app; the 27 guide slugs were read from the embedded page data.

denominators.name: NCCN Guidelines for Patients
denominators.notes: 77 patientGuidelineId entries with titles and version years read from the page HTML.

denominators.name: Patient Education Sheets (PES; ONS, NCODA, HOPA and ACCC; replaces the NCODA Oral Chemotherapy Education and IVE sheet sites)
denominators.notes: oralchemoedsheets.com returned 404; ons.org says PES replaces OCE and IVE with 'over 300 free, evidence-based education sheets'. NCODA's public WordPress API returned 990 resources, 522 of them PES sheets (links under ncoda.org/pes/). 443 of the 522 match an OnCo drug record by name.

coverage.method: URL match against the corpus URL index (cancer.gov paths normalised without query or anchor; ESMO, NCCN and PES links by domain and path). By library: PDQ 43/235 (18.3%; patient version 22/235, 9.4%); ESMO 3/27 (11.1%); NCCN 0/77; PES 0/522.
coverage.caveats: Linking is the measure; a summary could be paraphrased without a link, but no NCCN or PES item is named either. PDQ's screening (0/19), genetics (0/7) and integrative-therapy (0/24) summaries are entirely unlinked, as is 22 of 23 in supportive care.

notEnumerated: Macmillan and CRUK cancer information libraries: OnCo links them heavily (86 Macmillan cancer-information URLs) but no outside list of their pages was enumerated.

Cancer.Net (ASCO): https://www.cancer.net/cancer-types redirected to https://www.cancer.org/cancer/types.html on 2026-11-04, a JavaScript-rendered page; OnCo carries Cancer.Net as an alias on the American Cancer Society collection. ACS cancer-type guides were not enumerated.
Non-English national libraries (Krebsinformationsdienst, ganjoho.jp patient pages, kanker.nl, e-cancer.fr) were not enumerated; ganjoho.jp is linked only for statistics.
MedlinePlus (NLM) is MISSING in the corpus; not enumerated.
types.notes: The cheapest high-impact fill in this family: drug pages to PES sheets (443 matches by name), cancer pages to PDQ patient summaries and NCCN patient guidelines, symptom-paths.ts and side-effect-guidance.ts to the PDQ supportive-care summaries.

types.name: Germline hereditary cancer tests
types.oncoMethod: Test records (classify.py class 'test') for a germline product: bracanalysis-cdx only. The topic is carried by the technology record germline-testing, terms such as hereditary-cancer-syndromes, gbrca-mutation, lynch-syndrome, li-fraumeni, familial-pancreatic-cancer, germline-brca-testing-criteria-tnbc, risk-reducing-surgery-brca-carriers, and cancer records such as hereditary-ppgl, men2-syndrome, lynch-associated-colorectal-cancer and fap-associated-colorectal-cancer.

denominators.name: NIH Genetic Testing Registry (GTR) test_version.gz, current public tests filtered to hereditary cancer (test names and conditions)
denominators.notes: 63,425 current public GTR tests; 1,562 matched hereditary cancer names or conditions, from 120 laboratories (789 US). File dated 2026-11-01.

denominators.name: openFDA 510(k)/De Novo product codes QAZ (cancer predisposition risk assessment system, 866.6090) and QVU (high-throughput DNA sequencing for hereditary cancer predisposition, 866.6095); PMA product code PJG (cancer-related germline gene mutation detection system)
denominators.notes: Distinct products: 23andMe BRCA1/BRCA2 (Selected Variants) report (DEN170046, K223597), 23andMe HOXB13 prostate report (K211499), 23andMe MUTYH-Associated Polyposis (K182784), Invitae Common Hereditary Cancers Panel (DEN210011), BRACAnalysis CDx (P140020).

denominators.name: NHS England National genomic test directory for rare and inherited disease, version 9 (R codes for inherited cancer)
denominators.notes: 34 cancer-predisposition R codes (R207-R227, R229, R254, R295, R347, R363-R367, R404, R414, R422, R430, R456, R457); 31 used after excluding R404 (testing of unaffected relatives) and R456/R457 (germline-origin catch-alls).

denominators.name: Vendor menus: Natera oncology; Foundation Medicine solutions
denominators.notes: Natera lists 'Empower – Hereditary Cancer Test'; https://www.foundationmedicine.com/our-solutions lists FoundationOne Germline and FoundationOne PGx.

coverage.method: Named germline products: 5 FDA-authorised products (1 covered: BRACAnalysis CDx) plus 12 named multigene panels from major US labs, taken from GTR and two vendor menus (0 covered). Random sample: 0 of 60 seeded GTR hereditary-cancer tests (seed 20261104, 27 labs) match any OnCo test record. Syndrome level: 22 of 31 NHS inherited-cancer indications have a cancer, term or biomarker record (71.0%).
coverage.caveats: GTR names are lab-specific (many are single-gene tests), so test-level coverage will always be low; the gap is the named, widely ordered panels and the FDA direct-to-consumer reports, not every lab's catalogue.

notEnumerated: Full GTR test-level coverage: 1,562 lab tests; measured on a seeded sample of 60 only.
European and Asian commercial hereditary panels (e.g. CeGaT, Blueprint/Quest, MedGenome) beyond GTR registrations: not enumerated.
Polygenic risk scores sold as cancer risk tests (e.g. Myriad riskScore, Ambry AmbryScore): no register found; not enumerated.
types.notes: FDA germline products: 1 of 5 covered (BRACAnalysis CDx). Named major-lab panels: 0 of 12. Syndromes: 22 of 31 NHS inherited-cancer indications are covered by a record; the 9 not covered are R212, R215, R222, R224, R254, R295, R347, R366, R430 (hereditary prostate cancer at syndrome level; the hoxb13 gene record exists). Ambry RNAinsight is tagged for the RNA agent as germline RNA testing.

types.name: Complementary and alternative products
types.oncoMethod: Technology records defined in src/data/complementary.ts (56 tech() records graded with evidence:<grade> tags; the side-table count of 58 includes 2 non-record index entries), plus nutrition.ts records on supplements and diets (e.g. vitamin-d-omega3-supplementation, soy-breast-cancer, high-dose-vitamin-c, dietary-supplements-treatment-interactions, unproven-diet-claims) and src/data/ivermectin.ts. COMPLEMENTARY_INDEX also grades existing records (exercise, scalp cooling, diets).

denominators.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering 'About Herbs, Botanicals and Other Products' database (all letter pages)
denominators.notes: 48 listing pages (letters # and A-Z, 10 entries a page) parsed; 308 distinct entries (herbs, supplements, vitamins, TCM/Kampo formulas, alternative regimens).

denominators.name: NCI PDQ Integrative, Alternative and Complementary Therapies summaries (health professional versions)
denominators.notes: Includes summaries no longer being updated.

denominators.name: NCCIH Herbs at a Glance
denominators.notes: General-population herb fact sheets, not cancer-specific.

coverage.method: Each MSK entry checked with incorpus.py using the entry name, slug and (for 120 entries) Latin, trade and common aliases (e.g. Coriolus versicolor|turkey tail, Hoxsey, Gerson, silymarin). RECORD or IN-RECORD-NAME counted only after reading the matched record: 8 false hits removed (GCP -> ICH-GCP term, Calcium/Collagen/Leucine/Zinc/Folate -> gene targets, Chia -> Chia Tai Tianqing company, Chromium -> 10x Chromium, Coenzyme Q10 -> mitochondrial targets, Asian ginseng -> the American ginseng record). Second measures: NCI PDQ CAM summaries 14/24 (58.3%); NCCIH Herbs at a Glance 7/56 (12.5%).
coverage.caveats: About 14 covered entries count only because a trial or paper record is named for the product (e.g. astragalus, cordyceps, alpha-lipoic acid, DHEA, psilocybin, vitamin E), not because a graded complementary record exists. MSK also lists vitamins and minerals used as nutrition (calcium, magnesium, folate) that may be out of scope for a CAM page.

notEnumerated: MSK entry pages (evidence summaries per herb) were not read; only listing pages, so no grades were taken from MSK.
Mind-body and practitioner-based therapies beyond the PDQ list (e.g. chiropractic, naturopathy as a practice, cupping) were not enumerated against a list.
Commercial supplement products and clinics (e.g. specific 'integrative' clinics abroad) have no authoritative denominator.
types.notes: MSK's list contains 308 entries; 225 are named nowhere in OnCo. The highest-impact misses are herbs with interaction or bleeding risk that patients take during chemotherapy (milk thistle, echinacea, ginkgo, garlic, black cohosh, CoQ10, Asian ginseng) and alternative regimens promoted as cures (low-dose naltrexone, cesium chloride, insulin potentiation therapy, graviola). Full per-entry status: /tmp/gapcensus/work/medicines-practice/out/msk-check.json.

types.name: Reporting and data systems (BI-RADS, PI-RADS, Bethesda...)
types.oncoMethod: Term records whose subject is a reporting or categorisation system: pi-rads, li-rads, lung-rads, bethesda-category (thyroid), cin-hsil (cervical cytology categories). Related but counted elsewhere: deauville-score (response), gleason-grade-group (grading), pancreatic-cyst-high-risk-stigmata (Fukuoka/Kyoto criteria), pulmonary-nodule. The report reader (report-fields.ts, src/app/report-reader) explains pathology-report fields for 6 cancer groups (breast, prostate, colorectal, lung, lymphoma, myeloma).

In development: Brain Tumor RADS, KI-RADS. Collaborations: CAD-RADS (cardiac, excluded), I-TIRADS (publication pending). Th…

denominators.notes: 70 datasets in 12 site groups (the Ophthalmic group lists none in the index).

denominators.name: CAP Cancer Protocol Templates (current cancer protocols)
denominators.notes: 108 protocols incl. biomarker and generic templates; the April 2026 notes retire Pharynx and Major Salivary Glands, which the list still shows.

denominators.name: Cytopathology reporting systems (IAC, ASC, WHO-IARC series) and further imaging and endoscopy categorisation systems, each resolved to its defining publication on Crossref
denominators.notes: No single registry lists these; the set was assembled from the systems named in the assignment plus their siblings.

coverage.method: Each named system run through incorpus with its abbreviation and full name; covered = RECORD or IN-RECORD-NAME.

notEnumerated: ACR works in progress (Bone-RADS, Soft Tissue-RADS) and in development (Brain Tumor RADS, KI-RADS) were not counted: ACR states there is insufficient evidence for routine use.
Per-dataset ICCR and CAP gaps are summarised as two gaps (the standards themselves); a per-tumour list is in the work files.
types.notes: OnCo has only three of the nine oncology RADS that ACR lists (PI-RADS, LI-RADS, Lung-RADS); BI-RADS, the category on every mammogram report, is named once. No cytopathology system other than thyroid Bethesda and cervical HSIL/LSIL is named anywhere.

types.name: Hereditary cancer syndromes
types.oncoMethod: Pages whose subject is a syndrome or germline carrier state: cancer records men1-syndrome, men2-syndrome, multiple-endocrine-neoplasia, hereditary-ppgl, hyperparathyroidism-jaw-tumour-syndrome, lynch-associated-colorectal-cancer, fap-associated-colorectal-cancer, brca-associated-tnbc (8); term records hereditary-cancer-syndromes (overview), lynch-syndrome, lynch-syndrome-testing-uk, li-fraumeni, vhl-disease, men1-hereditary-net, inherited-skin-cancer-syndromes, familial-pancreatic-cancer, gbrca-mutation, sdh-deficiency, pten-loss (11, the last two biomarker terms whose aka name Carney-Stratakis/Carney triad and Cowden/PTEN hamartoma); biomarker brca-germline (1). bap1-loss term also names BAP1-TPDS in its aka. Found by name search of kinds term/cancer/biomarker plus the incorpus matches; cancer tag 'hereditary' has 2 records.

denominators.name: Orphanet classification of rare neoplastic diseases, branch 'Inherited cancer-predisposing syndrome' (Orphadata product3 id 202, CC-BY-4.0)
denominators.notes: 181 disorders in the branch (all types except categories/groups); 144 of DisorderType Disease or Malformation syndrome form the measured set. Sub-branches: polymalformative syndromes with cancer risk, lymphoproliferative (mostly inborn errors of immunity), digestive, haematologic, renal, NF/schwanno…

denominators.name: NHS England National Genomic Test Directory (rare and inherited disease, inherited cancer R-codes)
denominators.notes: HTTP 202 with a JavaScript robot check ('we need to verify that you're not a robot'); the XLSX link could not be reached.

denominators.name: GeneReviews (NCBI Bookshelf) and NCI PDQ cancer genetics summaries
denominators.notes: Not fetched this session (budget); Orphanet enumerates the field.

coverage.method: Every Disease/Malformation-syndrome entry in the Orphanet branch looked up with incorpus.py; the clinically important ones re-checked with hand-written aliases (hyphenation, 'associated' vs 'related', abbreviations). Covered = a page about the syndrome or a record whose name/aka names it (brief's RECORD / IN-RECORD-NAME rule); matches that hit only a gene target, a trial or a paper do not count.
coverage.caveats: About a third of the branch is inborn errors of immunity and developmental syndromes with a modest cancer risk (e.g. Alagille, Rubinstein-Taybi, combined immunodeficiencies); coverage of the syndromes oncology services test for routinely is much higher than the overall figure but still misses NF1, MUTYH polyposis, Peutz-Jeghers, HDGC and CMMRD.

notEnumerated: NHS National Genomic Test Directory: JavaScript robot check.
GeneReviews / NCI PDQ genetics: not attempted.
Gene-level predisposition without a named syndrome (e.g. CHEK2, PALB2, ATM, RAD51C/D moderate-penetrance genes) is not an Orphanet syndrome and was not measured here.

types.name: Navigation services
types.oncoMethod: Records: financial-navigation (technology). Freeman Patient Navigation Institute as one link; 'clinical nurse specialist' in 19 files and 'key worker' in 10, mostly UK first-60-days and spike text). Disease-charity navigators (PanCAN, LLS Information Specialists, FORCE peer navigation) are described in free-wave.ts.

coverage.method: WCRF matrix exposures checked with incorpus.py plus hand adjudication: covered = a record is about the exposure or its immediate parent (red meat and processed meat by red-processed-meat-reduction; coffee; sugar-sweetened drinks by ultra-processed-food-ssb; alcoholic drinks; Mediterranean pattern; glycaemic load by the glycaemic-index term; high-dose beta-carotene supplements by the CARET paper record; mate by the IARC Volume 116 paper record; physical activity and vigorous physical activity by energy-balance and exercise-oncology; adult body fatness by obesity-related-cancers; dietary fibre …

notEnumerated: The WCRF matrix's per-cancer judgements (which exposure is convincing or probable for which cancer) could not be read from the graphical PDF; the 2018 Third Expert Report summary (https://www.wcrf.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Summary-of-Third-Expert-Report-2018.pdf) holds the same matrix and could be read in a fill round to wire exposures to cancer pages.

types.notes: The largest reader-facing gaps are the three ECAC5 recommendations with no record at all (breastfeeding, hormone replacement therapy, work exposures) and vaping, which ECAC5 now names in its first recommendation.

types.name: Carcinogens (IARC)
types.oncoMethod: Every IARC Group 1 (135) and Group 2A (98) agent was checked with incorpus.py using the agent name plus synonyms (e.g. 'Ciclosporin|cyclosporine|cyclosporin', 'Tobacco, smokeless|smokeless tobacco|chewing tobacco|snuff|snus'), then each RECORD or IN-RECORD-NAME hit was read and adjudicated by hand. Covered = a record or side-table row is about the agent or its exposure class: 40 Group 1 agents (11 are cytotoxic or hormonal drug product records, e.g. cyclophosphamide, tamoxifen, melphalan; MOPP and BEP are rows in regimens.ts; infection terms hbv-hcv, ebv-term, hhv8-kshv, lymphoma-htlv-1, mcpyv-status, hpv-status; asbestos and radon terms; alcohol-attributable-cancer and alcohol-reduction-labelling; red-processed-meat-reduction; idea-prev-clean-air-never-smoker-endpoints for outdoor air pollution; sun-protection-after-skin-cancer and actinic-keratosis for solar UV; idea-prev-commercial-sunbed-ban; second-cancer-after-radiotherapy terms for X- and gamma-radiation) and 12 Group 2A agents (8 cytotoxic drug records such as cisplatin, doxorubicin, lomustine; red meat; very hot beverages via the IARC vol 116 paper and coffee-intake-cancer; night shift work via the IARC vol 124 paper; acrolein via the term second-primary-bladder-after-cyclophosphamide). Hits rejected as spurious: 'sunlight' is the SUNLIGHT trial, 'radium-226' is an Ac-225 supply idea, 'thorium' is actinium-225-supply, 'talc' is talc pleurodesis trials, 'cobalt' is cobalt-60 teletherapy, 'hydrazine' is the hydrazine-sulfate remedy, 'Opisthorchis' is a paper title.

denominators.name: IARC Monographs: List of Classifications (agents classified by the IARC Monographs, volumes 1 to 142)
denominators.notes: The HTML page has no CSV link; the table is built from a JavaScript object embedded in https://webapi.iarc.who.int/loc/loc.app.js (last_volume "142", last_update "2026-07-23 14:08 (CET)"), parsed to JSON. 1128 entries: Group 1 135, Group 2A 98, Group 2B 329, Group 3 498, and 68 cross-reference rows …

coverage.method: Group 1, full enumeration (135 agents): 40 covered, 36 MENTION, 59 MISSING after hand adjudication of incorpus hits (see onco.method). Group 2A, full enumeration rather than a sample (98 agents): 12 covered (12.2%), 8 MENTION, 78 MISSING. Combined Group 1 + 2A: 52 of 233 (22.3%).
coverage.caveats: Several IARC entries are facets of one exposure (alcoholic beverages, ethanol in and acetaldehyde from alcoholic beverages; four HPV rows; outdoor air pollution and its particulate matter) and were counted covered together. Drug records count as covered even where the record does not say the drug is a carcinogen. Many uncovered Group 1 entries are industrial chemicals with little direct patient relevance (e.g. 2,3,4,7,8-pentachlorodibenzofuran, magenta production); the gap list is ranked for reader impact, not taken in list order.

notEnumerated: Group 2B (329) and Group 3 (498): not measured; Group 2B holds many agents patients ask about (e.g. radiofrequency electromagnetic fields, aspartame) and could be sampled in a later round.
Target organs per agent (the IARC 'cancer sites with sufficient evidence' table) were not enumerated; it is a separate IARC PDF table and would let each cancer page list its established causes.
types.notes: The highest-value fix is probably one carcinogen record per exposure class (medicines, infections, diet, household air, occupational, environmental chemicals) carrying the IARC group and volume, then supplementing existing cancer pages; the three Volume 137 medicines (hydrochlorothiazide, tacrolimus, voriconazole) and the Volume 100A immunosuppressants ciclosporin and azathioprine can supplement the existing term skin-cancer-after-organ-transplant.

coverage.method: Denominator: distinct cancer or cancer-supportive medicines in a current FDA shortage (7, flurazepam excluded) or in an EMA shortage entry ongoing or updated since 2023 (13 more). 'Covered' = OnCo has a page about the entity: a cancer record by name or aka, the entity's own record for a site variant (e.g. inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour of the bladder -> IMT record), or a term page whose subjec…
coverage.caveats: The automated proximity search (all name tokens within 90 characters) proved about 65% precise on a seeded sample of 30, so every proximity-only hit (127) was adjudicated by hand. Exact-phrase mentions (whole word) were accepted without review apart from false hits found on inspection ('Brenner' matched a person, 'stump' matched a margin term). Level-2 nodes are main types (57% have a page); deeper levels are mostly histological variants and genetic subtypes.

types.notes: Where OnCo is thin (page coverage by OncoTree tissue): Skin 25%, Cervix 26%, Esophagus/Stomach 27%, Ovary/Fallopian Tube 28%, Bone 35%, Myeloid 38%, Liver 38%. Borderline ovarian tumours, skin adnexal carcinomas, gastrointestinal NETs outside pancreas and small bowel, plasmacytomas and the rarer myeloid neoplasms (CNL, CEL, MLN-TK) are the clearest clusters. Benign tumours are excluded from OnCo by stated policy (src/data/cancers-wave4-rare.ts), which explains part of the 'absent' tier (dermatofibroma, poroma, Brenner tumour, adenomas).

coverage.method: Brief's named list (35) checked with incorpus by name, abbreviation and aliases; RECORD means a record or term carries the score in its name or aka (or a side-table record names it). coverage.caveats: Strict (record or term carries it): 18/35. Lenient (named anywhere in src/data, which may satisfy the owner's link-out rule if the mention sits in a record): 30/35 (85.7%). Haematology prognostic indices are well covered; breast, lung and prostate risk calculators, nodule models, febrile-neutropenia and geriatric toxicity scores, and palliative prognostic scores are the weak branches. notEnumerated: MSK breast nomograms: blocked (403/404).
MDCalc oncology calculator list: not attempted (commercial site; not an authoritative denominator).
Broad catalogue of cancer risk prediction models (NCI DCCPS page 404); a systematic review that tabulates models by cancer site would be the next denominator to read.

Prostate biopsy risk calculators (ERSPC/Rotterdam, PCPT), hereditary models (BRCAPRO, MMRpro, Claus, Manchester score), comorbidity indices (Charlson, Elixhauser, Kaplan-Feinstein), transplant scores (EBMT, Disease Risk Index) and spinal metastasis scores (Tokuhashi, Tomita): corpus shows MISSING or MENTION, but no source was fetched this session, so they are not listed as gaps.
types.notes: The palliative prognostic scores here (PPI, PaP, PiPS) are the instruments behind the ESMO 2023 guideline topic 'Prognostic evaluation in patients with advanced cancer in the last months of life', listed under palliative-end-of-life.

denominators.name: COSMIC Mutational Signatures, Version 3.6 (SBS, DBS, ID, CN, SV index pages)
denominators.notes: Parsed signature cards from /signatures/sbs/, /dbs/, /id/, /cn/, /sv/: 186 signatures (SBS 101, DBS 22, ID 25, CN 26, SV 12), of which 23 are flagged as artefacts (19 SBS, 1 DBS, 3 CN). 163 real; 85 of them with a proposed aetiology other than 'Unknown'.

coverage.method: Non-artefact COSMIC v3.6 signatures named by id anywhere in src/data (read from snippets, including shorthand like 'sbs6/15/26'). With a record of their own: 2/163 (SBS88, ID18 via the colibactin term). Of the 85 with a known aetiology, about 15 are named.
coverage.caveats: Aetiologies themselves are often present under other names (tobacco, UV, APOBEC, MMR, HRD, platinum, temozolomide); the gap is the signature as a readable object that links a pattern in a tumour genome to its cause, including treatment-caused and inherited-repair-defect signatures.

notEnumerated: Per-signature pages (prevalence by cancer type, reference papers) were not fetched; only the five index pages were read.
types.notes: Signatures matter for patients mainly through HRD and MMR testing (ID6, SBS3, SBS21/26/44), inherited polyposis (SBS30 NTHL1, SBS36 MUTYH), exposures (SBS22 aristolochic acid, SBS24 aflatoxin, SBS29 chewing tobacco) and treatment-caused second cancers (SBS87 thiopurine, SBS99 melphalan, SBS31/35 platinum, SBS32 azathioprine).

coverage.sample: Seeded random sample of 60 of the 324 unmatched keys re-checked with incorpus.py: 28 MISSING, 22 named only in trial/paper record titles, 9 MENTION, 1 non-drug record; by hand about 7 were covered under another spelling or code (typos such as tilelizumab/pembolizumab, GB491 = lerociclib, Ris-Rez = hs-20089, regimens such as CHOP) and about 15 were noise or non-oncology (furosemide, deucravacitinib, efgartigimod, dose text). coverage.method: Distinct specific-agent keys matched to a drug or technology record. Trial-weighted: 3785/4209 agent-trial pairs (89.9%). By frequency: agents in >=2 trials 311/372 (83.6%); >=3 trials 200/216 (92.6%); >=5 trials 124/130 (95.4%).
